title: Trade the single-flag rate probe for seven-flag coverage in Production
notes: The bounded Production probe evaluates only the first flag a release owns, by design, so at two evaluators demo-email-notifications-v2 had full Production targeting and no Production caller. Its drain would have been unprovable in a critical environment, which is the heart of the archive story.

Under a connection budget the probe is poor value: one connection covering one flag against one covering seven. Switching demo-orders Production to the ordinary business-hours pattern costs no additional connection and restores coverage of all seven flags, including both the surviving archive candidate and all three false-silence controls.

What is lost is the 1200 evaluations per hour demonstration on demo-cart-v2. Volume was never the constraint and can be restored in September when the allowance resets; flag coverage in a critical environment cannot be recovered retroactively, because evaluation history is real elapsed time.
Found by reading the running probe output rather than the configuration. The traffic pattern was correct in the scenario and wrong for the purpose.
